items.stem: Define the term 'quality control'.
items.answer: Checking products at the end of production (or at stages) by inspectors to find and remove faulty items before they reach customers.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition, checking products at the end of production (or at stages) by inspectors to find and remove faulty items before they reach customers. 1 mark: partial definition or relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain why quality assurance may reduce costs compared with quality control.
items.answer: Preventing faults at each stage means less waste, rework and inspection at the end, and fewer returns and complaints.
items.markingKey: 1 mark prevention v detection; 1 mark cost saving. [2]

items.stem: Explain one way a business can measure the quality of a service.
items.answer: Customer satisfaction surveys, mystery shoppers, complaint rates, waiting times or repeat-customer rates.
items.markingKey: 1 mark method; 1 mark how it shows quality. [2]

items.stem: Lanka Tea Estates plc is a public limited company based in Colombo, Sri Lanka. It grows, processes and packs tea on its own estates and employs about 5,000 people. Many young workers are leaving the estates for jobs in the cities. Explain the benefits to Lanka Tea of moving from quality control to quality assurance.
items.answer: Points to develop for Lanka Tea: QA prevents faults at every stage; lower waste and inspection costs; empowered staff are more motivated; more consistent quality of packaged tea.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: QA prevents faults at every stage. AO2 Application [1]: answer uses the case (Lanka Tea: agriculture and food, about 5,000 employees, public limited company in Sri Lanka; many young workers are leaving the estates for jobs in the cities). AO3 Analysis [2]: developed chains of reasoning showing the consequence for Lanka Tea, e.g. lower waste and inspection costs; empowered staff are more motivated; more consistent quality of packaged tea. Levels: L1 knowledge only; L2 applied to the case; L3 applied and analysed. [4]

items.stem: Andina Solar SpA produced 120,000 units last month; 3,000 were rejected at inspection. Each unit costs $4 to make. Calculate the reject rate and the monthly cost of rejected units. A quality assurance system costing $10,000 a month would cut the reject rate to 1.5%. Calculate the net annual saving.
items.answer: 2.5%; $12,000 a month; net saving −$62,400

items.stem: Based in Cape Town, Cape Brew Co. (Pty) Ltd (private limited company) brews craft beers and low-sugar soft drinks sold through bars and supermarkets. The business has around 140 employees. Demand has grown faster than its small brewery can produce. Discuss the importance of quality to the competitiveness of Cape Brew.
items.answer: For: reputation and loyalty; premium pricing; lower costs of waste. Against: price may matter more to customers; improving quality is costly; other factors such as delivery speed. Judgement: the decision for Cape Brew depends mainly on its market positioning, and also on what competitors offer.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [2]: relevant concepts/theory. AO2 Application [2]: uses case evidence (Cape Brew: beverages, about 140 employees, private limited company in South Africa; demand has grown faster than its small brewery can produce). AO3 Analysis [4]: arguments for, e.g. reputation and loyalty; premium pricing; lower costs of waste; arguments against, e.g. price may matter more to customers; improving quality is costly; other factors such as delivery speed. AO4 Evaluation [4]: a supported judgement that weighs the arguments, e.g. it depends on its market positioning; what competitors offer; the cost of quality failures. Highest level needs a justified conclusion specific to Cape Brew, not a generic one. [12]

items.stem: What is the main difference between quality control and quality assurance?
options: Quality control is cheaper in every case
Quality assurance only checks finished products
Quality assurance aims to prevent faults; quality control aims to detect them
items.answer: Quality assurance aims to prevent faults; quality control aims to detect them
items.markingKey: Quality assurance aims to prevent faults; quality control aims to detect them. QA builds quality in at each stage; QC inspects and rejects faulty output.

items.stem: Battery supply problems from Asia have delayed several large orders. Tejo Mobility SA, a public limited company in Portugal with about 600 employees, assembles electric scooters and e-bikes for sale across the European Union. Explain one advantage to Tejo Mobility of replacing end-of-line inspection with a quality assurance system.
items.answer: Faults prevented, less waste.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: relevant advantage, e.g. faults prevented, less waste; workers take responsibility for quality; consistent quality builds reputation. 1 mark: explained in the context of Tejo Mobility (vehicle manufacturing). [2]

items.stem: Explain why improving quality can increase revenue as well as reduce costs.
items.answer: Higher quality builds reputation and loyalty, allows premium prices and generates repeat purchases and word-of-mouth.
items.markingKey: 1 mark reputation/loyalty; 1 mark premium price or more sales. [2]

items.stem: The owners want to double the number of cafés within three years. Café Cordillera SAS, a private limited company in Colombia with about 900 employees, roasts coffee and runs a chain of 60 cafés. (a) Define 'quality assurance'. (b) Explain one advantage to Café Cordillera of replacing end-of-line inspection with a quality assurance system.
items.answer: (a) A system that sets quality standards for every stage of production and makes all employees responsible for meeting them, so faults are prevented rather than detected. (b) Faults prevented, less waste.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark partial, 2 marks full definition [2] (b) 1 mark point (faults prevented, less waste; workers take responsibility for quality; consistent quality builds reputation), 1 mark explanation, 1 mark application to Café Cordillera [3]

items.stem: Define the term 'total quality management (TQM)'.
items.answer: An approach in which quality is the responsibility of every employee, every process aims at zero defects and the needs of internal and external customers are put first.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition, an approach in which quality is the responsibility of every employee, every process aims at zero defects and the needs of internal and external customers are put first. 1 mark: partial definition or relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain why kaizen depends on employee involvement.
items.answer: Ideas for small improvements come from workers who know the processes best; they must be trained, empowered and motivated to suggest and implement changes.
items.markingKey: 1 mark employees as source of ideas; 1 mark need for empowerment/motivation. [2]

items.stem: Explain two difficulties of introducing TQM.
items.answer: Requires a change of culture and long-term commitment; training costs; resistance from staff and managers; results take time.
items.markingKey: 2 × (1 mark difficulty, 1 mark explanation). [4]

items.stem: A major US retailer has asked it to cut delivery times from twelve weeks to six. items.answer: Points to develop for Mekong Furniture: kaizen = continuous small improvements; employees suggest ways to cut waste; small savings add up over time; improves processes without large investment.

items.answer: TQM relies on trained, involved and empowered staff who take responsibility, which fits the soft HRM view of employees as assets.

items.stem: Define the term 'benchmarking'.
items.answer: Comparing a business's products, processes or performance with those of the best firms in the industry (or other industries) in order to identify improvements.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition, comparing a business's products, processes or performance with those of the best firms in the industry (or other industries) in order to identify improvements. 1 mark: partial definition or relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain one limitation of benchmarking.
items.answer: Information on competitors may be hard to obtain; copying others does not create a unique advantage; what works elsewhere may not suit the business's culture.
items.markingKey: 1 mark limitation; 1 mark explanation. [2]

items.stem: Explain why ISO 9000 certification does not guarantee high-quality products.
items.answer: It certifies that procedures are followed and documented, not that the product standard is high; firms can consistently produce average quality.
items.markingKey: 1 mark certifies systems; 1 mark not product quality. [2]

items.answer: Points to develop for Muscat Dates: ISO 9000 certifies a quality management system; reassures overseas buyers of packed dates and date syrup; can win contracts that require certification; documented procedures improve consistency.

items.stem: Nile Pharma plc is a public limited company based in Cairo, Egypt. Explain how a kaizen approach could reduce costs at Nile Pharma.
items.answer: Points to develop for Nile Pharma: kaizen = continuous small improvements; employees suggest ways to cut waste; small savings add up over time; improves processes without large investment.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: kaizen = continuous small improvements. AO2 Application [1]: answer uses the case (Nile Pharma: pharmaceuticals, about 1,800 employees, public limited company in Egypt; most of its raw ingredients are imported and paid for in US dollars). AO3 Analysis [2]: developed chains of reasoning showing the consequence for Nile Pharma, e.g. employees suggest ways to cut waste; small savings add up over time; improves processes without large investment. Levels: L1 knowledge only; L2 applied to the case; L3 applied and analysed. [4]

items.stem: Deccan Auto Components Ltd produces 100,000 units a year and its defect rate is 4%. Each defect costs $10 to put right. TQM training costing $120,000 is expected to cut the defect rate to 1%. Calculate the annual saving.

Based in Singapore, Lumen Robotics plc (public limited company) designs and builds robots used on factory assembly lines. The business has around 2,400 employees. Shareholders are pressing for higher dividends while engineers want more spending on research. Explain how introducing TQM could improve the competitiveness of Lumen Robotics.
items.answer: Points to develop for Lumen Robotics: TQM makes quality everyone's responsibility; fewer defects lower costs of industrial robots; improved reputation and customer loyalty; motivated staff through involvement.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: TQM makes quality everyone's responsibility. AO2 Application [1]: answer uses the case (Lumen Robotics: industrial engineering, about 2,400 employees, public limited company in Singapore; shareholders are pressing for higher dividends while engineers want more spending on research). AO3 Analysis [2]: developed chains of reasoning showing the consequence for Lumen Robotics, e.g. fewer defects lower costs of industrial robots; improved reputation and customer loyalty; motivated staff through involvement. Levels: L1 knowledge only; L2 applied to the case; L3 applied and analysed. [4]

items.stem: Based in Karachi, Indus Sports Goods Ltd (private limited company) makes hand-stitched and machine-stitched footballs and cricket equipment. The business has around 950 employees. items.stem: Pearl Logistics WLL benchmarks its performance against the best firm in its industry — customer satisfaction score (out of 10): Pearl Logistics 7, benchmark 8.8; defect rate (%): Pearl Logistics 6, benchmark 2; average order processing time (hours): Pearl Logistics 36, benchmark 18. Calculate the percentage gap between Pearl Logistics and the benchmark for each measure.
items.answer: customer satisfaction score (out of 10) +25.7%; defect rate (%) -66.7%; average order processing time (hours) -50.0%

items.stem: Andina Solar SpA is a private limited company based in Santiago, Chile. It designs and installs solar power systems for farms, mines and homes and employs about 380 people. The government has announced new subsidies for business investment in renewable energy. Evaluate whether Andina Solar should apply for ISO 9000 certification.
items.answer: For: customer confidence; access to contracts; better systems. Against: costs of audit and documentation; no guarantee of product quality; bureaucracy. Judgement: the decision for Andina Solar depends mainly on whether customers demand it, and also on the cost relative to benefits.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [3]: relevant concepts/theory. AO2 Application [3]: uses case evidence (Andina Solar: renewable energy, about 380 employees, private limited company in Chile; the government has announced new subsidies for business investment in renewable energy). AO3 Analysis [6]: arguments for, e.g. customer confidence; access to contracts; better systems; arguments against, e.g. costs of audit and documentation; no guarantee of product quality; bureaucracy. AO4 Evaluation [8]: a supported judgement that weighs the arguments, e.g. it depends on whether customers demand it; the cost relative to benefits; what competitors hold. Highest level needs a justified conclusion specific to Andina Solar, not a generic one. [20]

items.stem: Which of the following best defines 'total quality management (TQM)'?
options: Comparing a business's products, processes or performance with those of the best firms in the industry (or other industries) in order to identify improvements.
A system that sets quality standards for every stage of production and makes all employees responsible for meeting them, so faults are prevented rather than detected.
An approach in which quality is the responsibility of every employee, every process aims at zero defects and the needs of internal and external customers are put first.
An international quality standard awarded to organisations that have a quality management system meeting set requirements, checked by independent audit.
items.answer: An approach in which quality is the responsibility of every employee, every process aims at zero defects and the needs of internal and external customers are put first.
items.markingKey: total quality management (TQM): An approach in which quality is the responsibility of every employee, every process aims at zero defects and the needs of internal and external customers are put first.

items.stem: Based in Auckland, Kiwi Trails Ltd (private limited company) runs guided hiking, kayaking and cycling tours. The business has around 90 employees. Bookings are highly seasonal and most guides are employed only for the summer. (a) Define 'ISO 9000'. (b) Explain one advantage to Kiwi Trails of benchmarking its processes against the best firms in its industry. (c) Analyse how benchmarking could improve the performance of Kiwi Trails. (d) Discuss whether benchmarking is the best way for Kiwi Trails to improve quality.
items.answer: (a) An international quality standard awarded to organisations that have a quality management system meeting set requirements, checked by independent audit. (b) Identifies best practice to copy or adapt. (c) Benchmarking compares performance with the best; identifies gaps in cost, quality or speed; adopting best practice improves efficiency; targets based on evidence motivate staff. (d) For: learns from best practice; evidence-based targets; faster than trial and error. Against: TQM and kaizen build quality from within; data hard to obtain; copying limits innovation. Judgement: the decision for Kiwi Trails depends mainly on availability of comparable firms, and also on the culture of the business.
